_note: PLACEHOLDER questions/weights — for format demonstration only. Sharon (RN) to author and approve the real Concern Check. This is the question POOL; each situation selects a subset via its 'questions' list. At least one caregiver-health question is included per the locked direction.

questions.prompt: In the last 3 months, has your parent fallen?
questions.help: A slip, a stumble, or being found on the floor all count.

questions.prompt: Did any fall lead to an injury, or a time they couldn't get up?
Is your parent noticeably weaker, slower, or less steady than before?
Have you noticed weight loss, or less interest in eating?
Have you noticed new memory, confusion, or judgment changes?
Has your parent made choices that seem unsafe (leaving the stove on, falling for scams, getting lost)?
Is your parent having trouble managing medications (missed doses, confusion, refills)?
Are there signs the home is becoming harder to manage (clutter, spoiled food, unopened mail)?
Is your parent having more difficulty with everyday tasks (cooking, dressing, bathing, bills)?
Have you noticed a decline in personal hygiene or grooming?
Does your parent seem more sad, anxious, or withdrawn than usual?
Is your parent seeing friends or family less than they used to?
When you offer help, does your parent refuse or insist everything is fine?
How often do you feel overwhelmed caring for or worrying about your parent?
questions.help: Your well-being is part of this picture too.

questions.prompt: Do you have enough support from family or others in caring for your parent?

questions._note: Falls-pathway-specific fork of falls-recent (12-month window vs. 3-month). Kept as a separate id so unsafe-alone / something-feels-different, which still use falls-recent, are unaffected.
questions.prompt: Has your parent fallen in the past 12 months?
questions.help: A slip, a stumble, or being found on the floor all count.

questions._note: Multi-select red-flag checklist. Feeds BOTH the numeric score (as the worst selected item's weight, not a sum — see lib/scoring.ts) and the emergency-trigger layer (see fall-severe-symptoms in emergency-triggers.json). Replaces the old binary fall-injury question for this pathway.
questions.prompt: Did any fall cause an injury, involve hitting their head, or leave them unable to get up without help?
questions.help: Select everything that applies to any fall in the past 12 months.

options.label: No — they were not hurt and got up on their own
Seemed more confused than usual afterward
Unusually drowsy or hard to wake
New weakness, or trouble speaking, walking, or seeing

questions._note: Falls-pathway-specific fork of mobility-change (exact wording per Sharon). Kept separate so moving-in, which still uses mobility-change, is unaffected.
questions.prompt: Has your parent become noticeably weaker, slower, or less steady when standing or walking?
Are they holding onto furniture or walls, appearing unsteady, or avoiding activities because they're afraid of falling?

questions._note: Falls-specific home hazards, distinct from the general home-management 'home-hazards' question (clutter/mail/spoiled food) used by other situations.
questions.prompt: Are there fall-specific hazards in the home — loose rugs, poor lighting, difficult stairs, cluttered walking paths, or lack of bathroom support (grab bars, non-slip mats)?

questions._note: Pure context per Sharon: important for a falls assessment but must not, by itself, move the score or fire any trigger. Deliberately excluded from every situation's scoringQuestions that uses it (weights are all 0) and not referenced by any emergency trigger.
questions.prompt: Does your parent live alone?

options.label: No — someone else is usually home

questions._note: Captures the DISCOVERY circumstances of a fall (how it was found), distinct from fall-severity which captures physical/medical symptoms. Per Sharon: should raise concern (see found-on-floor-concern trigger, targets take-action-soon, NOT get-immediate-help) without being able to independently force an emergency — only an actual fall-severity red flag does that.
questions.prompt: Was your parent found on the floor after a fall?
questions.help: This is about how the fall was discovered — the questions above already cover how they're doing physically.

options.label: No — they didn't end up on the floor, or got up right away
Yes, but they were found quickly and were okay
Yes, and they could not call or reach anyone for help
Yes, and they could not get up without help
Yes, and they may have been on the floor for a while (not sure how long)
